lesson.text: Remember? A word can have a root: its main part, like kind, help or play. Today we add parts to roots, and we clap out the beats in long words.
A prefix goes at the start and changes the meaning. un- means not (unkind). re- means again (replay). dis- means not, or the opposite (disagree). pre- means before (preview).
A suffix goes at the end. -ful means full of (helpful). -less means without (helpless). -ly means in that way (kindly). -er can mean a person who (player). -able means can be (washable).
Put them together: unhelpful = un (not) + help + ful (full of), so it means not helpful. To read a new word, take off its prefix and suffix and find the root.
Syllables are the beats in a word. Clap them: cat (1), gar-den (2), but-ter-fly (3), cat-er-pil-lar (4). Every syllable has a vowel sound.
Break long words into syllables to read and spell them: re-mem-ber, fan-tas-tic, hel-i-cop-ter.
Try it in the world: name things in your world with prefixes and suffixes: a rebuilt house, a helpful buddy, a fearless climb. Clap the syllables of each. Next: spelling patterns.

exercises.hint: Think of a replay of a game: you play it… how many times?
exercises.explain: re- means again: replay means play again.

exercises.prompt: A suffix goes at the end of a word.
exercises.explain: True: suffixes go at the end; prefixes go at the start.

exercises.prompt: What is the root word of "replaying"?
exercises.hint: Take off the prefix and the suffix.
exercises.explain: Take off re- and -ing and you have the root: play.

exercises.prompt: Which word means the opposite of "agree"?

exercises.hint: Think of preview: a look before.
exercises.explain: pre- means before, as in preview and preheat.
Take it apart: un (not) + help + ful (full of). Helpful means full of help, so unhelpful means not helpful.

exercises.hint: Clap each beat as you say it: cat, er, pil, lar.

exercises.prompt: Build the word "unbreakable" from its parts.
exercises.hint: The prefix comes first and the suffix last.
exercises.explain: un + break + able = unbreakable: it cannot be broken.
-able means can be, so wash + able = washable: it can be washed, like a washable coat.
-er can mean a person who does something: play + er = player, a person who plays. A builder builds and a singer sings.
False: pre- means before, so preheat means heat before.

exercises.prompt: Match each prefix or suffix to its meaning.
exercises.hint: Think of unkind, replay, preview and fearless.
exercises.explain: un- means not, re- again, pre- before and -less without.

exercises.prompt: Clap the beats in "unbelievable". How many syllables does it have?
exercises.hint: Take off the prefix and the suffix, clap each part, then put them back together.
exercises.explain: un-be-liev-a-ble: 5 syllables. It is un (not) + believe + able (can be), so it means so surprising you can hardly believe it.
